Let $X$ be the number of trees (out of 5) that fall on the line. Then $X \sim B\!\left(5, \tfrac{1}{10}\right)$.

$$P(X = 0) = \left(\frac{9}{10}\right)^5 = 0.59049 = 0.5905\ \text{(4 d.p.)}$$

fewer than three trees will fall on the line.
One hundred of such trees are cut near the line. Use the Normal approximation, to find to 2 significant figures, the probability that between 6 and 14 trees inclusive will fall on the line.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $Y$ be the number of trees (out of 100) that fall on the line: $Y \sim B\!\left(100, \tfrac{1}{10}\right)$.

Since $n$ is large and $np = 10$, $nq = 90$ are both greater than 5, approximate $Y$ by a Normal variable $W$ with

$$\mu = np = 10,\qquad \sigma^2 = npq = 100\times 0.1\times 0.9 = 9,\qquad \sigma = 3$$

**Continuity correction** (discrete to continuous): $P(6 \le Y \le 14)$ becomes $P(5.5 < W < 14.5)$.

$$z_1 = \frac{5.5 - 10}{3} = -1.5,\qquad z_2 = \frac{14.5 - 10}{3} = 1.5$$

$$P = \Phi(1.5) - \Phi(-1.5) = 2\Phi(1.5) - 1 = 2(0.9332) - 1 = 0.8664$$

**$P(6 \le Y \le 14) \approx 0.87$** (2 s.f.).

(Check: the exact binomial sum is $0.8699 \approx 0.87$.)
